title: The popes' bull against the Louvain doctor confirms Estius and Vázquez
source_text: XXX. Caeterum ista Gulielmi Estii & Gabrielis Vasquez sententia Pontificum Romanorum calculo comprobatur. Si quidem opposita doctrina damnata esse videtur in Bulla edita a Pio V. & a Gregorio XIII. confirmata. Nam inter alias propositiones quae in ea Bulla damnatae sunt, contra Doctorem quendam Lovaniensem, una est his verbis concepta. Omnia opera infidelium sunt peccata, & Philosophorum virtutes sunt vitia. Ut testatur Vasquez loco jam allegato.
pass_a_gloss: XXX. However that opinion of William Estius and Gabriel Vasquez is approved by the vote of the Roman Pontiffs. Since the opposite doctrine seems to have been condemned in the Bull issued by Pius V and confirmed by Gregory XIII. For among other propositions which were condemned in that Bull, against a certain Doctor of Louvain, one is conceived in these words. All the works of unbelievers are sins, and the virtues of the Philosophers are vices. As Vasquez testifies in the place already alleged.
pass_b_english: The popes of Rome have given their verdict for this view of Estius and Vázquez. The contrary teaching appears to stand condemned in Pius V's bull, which Gregory XIII later confirmed.

That bull, aimed at a Louvain doctor, condemns several propositions, and one of them reads: 'All the works of unbelievers are sins, and the virtues of the philosophers are vices.' Vázquez reports this in the passage cited above.

choices.why: One without faith; in XXVIII Estius narrows it to the pagan who lacks knowledge even of the one God, so 'unbeliever' with 'pagan' and 'heathen' where the text specifies.
